blocking.title: Gate logic now depends on isFullSha in apps/server/src/lib/github.ts, outside the three D4 ④ gate-source locations
blocking.evidence:
Rule: ADR 0021 D4 ④ says gate source lives only in apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/**, packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts and apps/daemon/src/merge-decision.ts ("闸的新源码不得放到别处，否则这一类按名判不到它"). Spec 28 §4 P3 says the same: gate code placed elsewhere is treated as ordinary product source and auto-merged.

Before this PR, every runtime value the merge-gate modules used came from those locations: @pacman/shared constants in records/merge-gate.ts and sibling merge-gate files. At the head, readiness.ts:20 imports isFullSha from ../../lib/github.js, defined at lib/github.ts:118-123 as FULL_SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/. The gate uses it for its new decisions:
- line 227: PR head, which gives pr-unreadable;
- line 256: check SHAs, which give required-checks-unreadable;
- line 356: compare SHAs, which give compare-malformed.

Why D4 misses it: lib/github.ts matches AUTO_MERGE_PATH_GLOBS 'apps/*/src/**' and appears in neither PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS nor MERGE_GATE_SOURCE_GLOBS (packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts:63-130). The same holds for pr-gate.js AUTO_MERGE and its gate-source list (lines 36, 95-96).

The file is actively edited by non-gate lanes: open PR #1489 (P2) changes it, and the spec 28 §8 P2 row plans a segment 3 there. /code-review raised this import twice (s2-r10-reviews.txt pass 1 finding 7, pass 2 finding 7) as layering only. The PR's Risk section keeps it for "no import-time effects" and does not address D4 ④.
blocking.failurePath:
1. A later lane PR touches only apps/server/src/lib/github.ts. For example, it relaxes FULL_SHA to accept abbreviated, uppercase or SHA-256 IDs for the compare URL builder, and adjusts merge-gate-readiness.test.ts, which is an auto-mergeable test path.
2. classifyPaths (paths.ts:54-56) and pr-gate.js both classify the change as plain product source. No protected-path or gate-source hit forces a human.
3. Today, under spec 28 D7, that PR is auto-merged after a pr-gate go. Under P4's autonomous policy it would be merged by the gate's own executor.
4. The merge changes which pr.headSha, check SHAs and compare SHAs mergeReadiness accepts. An abbreviated PR head would no longer give pr-unreadable, and that change lands without the user merge D4 ④ requires for any gate change. This is the 'agent changes the gate to pass it' risk ADR 0021 lists.

Fix that keeps the reuse: move FULL_SHA/isFullSha into packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts, which is protected, and have both lib/github.ts and readiness.ts import it from @pacman/shared. Alternatively, keep a local predicate inside merge-gate/.
skeptics:
I traced the failure path at 1174ebffd35b2bec7379e4f49f722ae01763a6f0 and it is real.

1. The import is new in this PR. In the diff, readiness.ts gains `import { isFullSha } from '../../lib/github.js';` at line 20. The other merge-gate modules import nothing outside merge-gate/ except @pacman/shared and node:crypto: digest.ts, paths.ts and evidence-link.ts each import only @pacman/shared, plus each other or node:crypto. Every runtime value those modules import from @pacman/shared, such as EVIDENCE_PREFIX, GATE_LIMITS, MERGE_BLOCKERS, MERGE_GATE_STATUS_CONTEXT and the path globs, is defined in packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts.

2. The helper now drives new gate decisions:
   - line 227 decides `head`, and a malformed head gives pr-unreadable, with headSha and patchDigest reported as null;
   - line 256 gives required-checks-unreadable for check SHAs;
   - line 356 gives compare-malformed for compare SHAs.
   `head` also gates the head-binding comparisons and the evidence-link judgement.

3. The helper sits outside the protected locations. FULL_SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ and isFullSha are at apps/server/src/lib/github.ts:118-123.
   - lib/github.ts matches AUTO_MERGE_PATH_GLOBS 'apps/*/src/**'. It is in neither PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS nor MERGE_GATE_SOURCE_GLOBS (packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts).
   - classifyPaths builds PROTECTED_RE and GATE_SOURCE_RE from those lists only (paths.ts).
   - pr-gate.js on main lists only the merge-gate paths (lines 95-96) besides AUTO_MERGE (line 36).
   So a PR that touches only lib/github.ts plus apps/server/test/** forces no human merge.

4. The file is shared and has its own reasons to change. isFullSha is also used by the compare URL builder (lib/github.ts:255) and by services/ci-loop.ts:625. A non-gate lane could plausibly relax FULL_SHA, for example to accept abbreviated or uppercase SHAs. That change would silently alter which heads, check SHAs and compare SHAs mergeReadiness accepts, without the user merge D4 ④ requires.

5. The rules forbid this. ADR 0021 D4 ④ says gate source lives only in the three locations: "闸的新源码不得放到别处，否则这一类按名判不到它". Spec 28 §4 line 118 says "放到别处的闸代码会被当成普通产品源码自动合并". The PR body's Risk section keeps the import only for "no import-time effects" and does not address D4 ④.

The finding's fix is sound: move the predicate into packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts or a local predicate under merge-gate/.

I deleted the private refs afterward.

I traced the failure path at 1174ebf and could not refute it.

(1) readiness.ts:20 imports isFullSha from ../../lib/github.js. The gate's new decisions run on that function: line 227 (a malformed head gives pr-unreadable), line 256 (check SHAs give required-checks-unreadable) and line 356 (compare SHAs give compare-malformed). isFullSha is defined at lib/github.ts:118-123 as FULL_SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.

(2) At base, no merge-gate module imported anything at runtime from outside @pacman/shared or its sibling files. readiness.ts imported only @pacman/shared, ./digest, ./evidence-link and ./paths. The predicate arrived in this PR's round 10 (commit 0cd8b31): a local isSha helper was swapped for the lib/github import after a /code-review reuse suggestion (s2-r10-reviews.txt, pass 1 finding 7). The same file records the layering objection in pass 2 finding 7 and keeps the import because it has "no import-time effect". That answer does not address D4 ④.

(3) ADR 0021 D4 ④ restricts gate source to three places, and spec 28 line 118 says gate code placed elsewhere is treated as plain product source and auto-merged. apps/server/src/lib/github.ts matches AUTO_MERGE_PATH_GLOBS 'apps/*/src/**'. It is in neither PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS (category ⑤ lists only secret-box, keys, token-auth and attachments-token under lib/) nor MERGE_GATE_SOURCE_GLOBS (packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts:63-130). pr-gate.js on main also lists none of it, so classifyPaths and pr-gate both treat a lib/github.ts-only PR as auto-mergeable.

(4) Relaxing FULL_SHA there would change which PR-head, check and compare SHAs mergeReadiness accepts. An abbreviated head would no longer give pr-unreadable. The test that pins this is in apps/server/test, also an auto-merge path, so a lane can edit it alongside without a test-deleted block.

The repo has kept gate-specific parsing inside the protected set elsewhere: compareFilesFromResponse lives in merge-gate/digest.ts, and evidence-link.ts keeps its own inline SHA regex. That makes the outside import here a real gap and not house style.

Two mitigating facts: mergeReadiness has no production caller yet (S4 and S6a are unbuilt), and GitHub always returns 40-hex SHAs. These lower the near-term impact but do not remove the structural D4 ④ hole at this head.

suggestions.title: A paged compare binds the commits to the head, but the files come from page 1 only; the contract does not say which page's total_commits counts
suggestions.evidence: Docstring lines 114-115: 'totalCommits = 响应的 total_commits（各页合起来的条数）'. Lines 123: '2 出自响应本身：外壳按分支名或从缓存读、却照 pr.headSha 填了 headSha，也认得出'. docs/verify/1404/s2-r10-github-shapes.txt section 2b/2c: 'files appear only on page 1'. Code at 360-374 checks commits.length === totalCommits and compareHead(commits) === head; the digest at 379 is computed from compare.files.
suggestions.failurePath: Multi-page compare (more commits than per_page) read by branch name or through a per-URL cache, which the docstring names as a threat it detects. Page 1, which carries the files and the first commits, is fresh at descendant D. Page 2 is a stale cached copy from when the branch was at H. If D is chronologically last, page 1's commits are the same as H's first page. The combined list is then exactly H's list, with n entries and no repeats, and compareHead returns H. If the shell takes totalCommits from the last page (n), the list counts as complete. With the PR response also at H, the gate computes D from D's files and labels it with head H, which is the round-9 class of mismatch. A shell that requests by SHA, as the contract asks, cannot hit this. It can be closed by making the S4 contract require that totalCommits come from page 1 (the page with files) and that every page report the same total_commits, otherwise 'unreadable'. Not blocking because there is no caller yet and it needs a contract-violating shell.

suggestions.title: Deterministic shell SHA faults are classed inconsistently: a malformed PR head is transient, a malformed compare SHA is human, and a contract-following shell turns the first into the second
suggestions.evidence: Line 231: block('pr-unreadable', 'head SHA not 40 lowercase hex') (transient). Lines 354-358: a malformed compare.headSha gives block('compare-malformed', ...) (human), justified at 133-135 as '写错的 SHA 每次读都一样，不该成为永远对不上的可等'. The same argument applies to a malformed pr.headSha, which is kept transient (Risk section).
suggestions.failurePath: pr.headSha is an uppercase SHA. A shell following the by-SHA contract either puts the same SHA in compare.headSha (giving human compare-malformed at 358) or passes 'malformed' (giving human compare-malformed at 353). So the 'transient, the gate waits' outcome that the test 'PR 的 head 写错只少了 head' pins (which pairs a malformed PR head with a lowercase compare.headSha) does not happen with a real shell. The result class depends on which input the shell got wrong first. Not a pass path, since both block, but S5-S9 route by class.

Line 208: compare-malformed label '读到了 compare，响应形状不对' now also covers the shell's own requested compare.headSha, which is not part of the response (readiness.ts:356). required-checks-unreadable at 190 was reworded for its new causes. suggestions.title: Verbatim verdict JSON contains a closing keyword followed by an issue number ("can close #1404")
suggestions.evidence: The added file's evidence string reads: "No commit message contains a closing keyword, so neither path can close #1404 by mistake." The dimension asks for no keyword+number form anywhere outside the intended closing line, and negations count. The PR's Risk section discloses it and says files are not parsed.
suggestions.failurePath: No failure at this head: GitHub parses closing keywords only in commit messages and PR/issue bodies, not in repository files, and this text is in none of them. It becomes live only if someone copies this verdict text into a commit message or PR body, for example while quoting evidence in a squash body. That would close #1404 before the last P3 segment. If the verbatim copy is kept, the commit message and squash body should keep quoting the file by path, not by content.

suggestions.title: Foreign-commit test only places the foreign commit after HEAD; a 'take the last tip' compareHead passes all 222 tests
suggestions.failurePath: I replaced readiness.ts:165 `return tips.length === 1 ? (tips[0]?.sha ?? null) : null;` with `return tips.length > 0 ? (tips[tips.length - 1]?.sha ?? null) : null;`. That accepts any number of tips and keeps the last listed one. Under that change the readiness and snapshot tests still pass 222 of 222. The test for a foreign commit in the list only uses `[...chain(EARLIER, HEAD), {sha: OTHER, parents:[MAIN]}]`, where OTHER comes after HEAD, so the last tip is OTHER and the read is blocked anyway. Concrete case the suite misses: a compare read at NEWER, where paging lost NEWER and put OTHER before HEAD, with the count equal to totalCommits. The tips are {OTHER, HEAD}, and the mutated code takes HEAD, so NEWER's files and digest would be judged as HEAD's and the gate would report ready. The head code is correct because it requires exactly one tip. The 'exactly one tip' rule is only pinned for one ordering. Adding a sub-case with OTHER listed before HEAD closes the gap.

suggestions.title: Empty compare commit list (totalCommits 0) has no test, although Risk says it blocks transiently
suggestions.failurePath: At the head, `compare.commits = []` with `totalCommits = 0` and `compare.headSha = HEAD` passes the format check and the completeness check. Then compareHead([]) returns null, which is not HEAD, so it gives patch-unavailable 'compare not read at the PR head'. The PR body's Risk section names this 'empty commit list' case as transient on purpose. No test pins it. I added `compare.commits.length > 0 &&` in front of the head-binding condition at line 370, so an empty list skips binding and is judged on the shell's label alone. The 222 tests still pass. A test like '不抛' at line 711 uses chain(HEAD) and never an empty list. A shell that sends an empty list from a stale or wrong read could therefore lose this rule in a later refactor with no test going red.

suggestions.title: Gate SHA validation now depends on isFullSha in apps/server/src/lib/github.ts, outside the D4 class-4 paths
suggestions.failurePath: ADR 0021 D4 class 4 says the gate's source lives only in apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/**, packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts and apps/daemon/src/merge-decision.ts (MERGE_GATE_SOURCE_GLOBS, records/merge-gate.ts:126-130), so that it can be judged by name. Before this PR, every runtime import of the gate modules came from records/merge-gate.ts, plus the type-only Phase. This PR adds `import { isFullSha } from '../../lib/github.js'` (readiness.ts:20) and uses it for the PR head (line 227), the check SHAs (line 256) and the compare SHAs (line 356). The regex behind it is FULL_SHA at apps/server/src/lib/github.ts:118. That path is in the auto-mergeable set (apps/*/src/**) and in no protected class (not class 4 and not class 5). The failure path: a later PR loosens FULL_SHA (for example to accept abbreviated or uppercase SHAs, or anything at all). classifyPaths raises no protected-path blocker for lib/github.ts, so under an autonomous policy that PR can merge without a person, and the gate's malformed-SHA rules change silently. The equality checks on head, compare.headSha, compareHead and the check SHAs still bind the result, so I traced no path to ready=true for a wrong patch, which is why this is a suggestion. Options: move the 40-hex check into records/merge-gate.ts or merge-gate/** (or re-export it from there for both callers), or add lib/github.ts to the class-4 globs and the ADR text.

For a complete base...head list from one read, every listed commit except head has a listed child (the next commit on a path from head cannot be on the base side). So the only tip is the commit the list was read at. This also holds when there are several merge bases. I checked it live on this PR's own compare (24 commits, including the merge commit 1813905e with a base-side parent): the tip is 1174ebff. Old, descendant and foreign-substitute reads are rejected, and a commit at head that is itself a merge is accepted. Each branch sets compare to null, so D, the paths, the evidence links and the verdicts are not judged against a compare that was rejected. (3) checks: the request SHA, statusSha and every runs[].headSha must be valid and equal head, and the list must be complete. When unstable with checks unreadable, the existing mergeable-state detail is kept. The self-required refactor into the loop gives the same output. The required-checks-unreadable detail for an incomplete list is unchanged from base. (4) When the head is null (PR null or a malformed head), pr-unreadable always blocks, so ready can never be true. The result's headSha and patchDigest are null, and changedFiles and the evidence links are not judged against an unbound compare. (5) No path gives ready=true unless compare.headSha, the compare's own head and all check SHAs equal pr.headSha. CI check runs on the head are all success.
